contains-duplicate.goal: Determine whether any value occurs more than once.
contains-duplicate.approach: Insert values into a set; encountering a value already present proves a duplicate. A sorted scan is an alternative.
contains-duplicate.edge: Empty input and duplicates far apart.

valid-anagram.goal: Check whether two strings have the same character multiset.
valid-anagram.approach: Count characters and compare frequencies after checking equal lengths. For lowercase English, use 26 counters.

two-sum.goal: Return distinct indices whose values add to a target.
two-sum.approach: For each value, look for target minus value in a map of earlier indices. Check before inserting to prevent using one index twice.

group-anagrams.goal: Group words with identical character multisets.
group-anagrams.approach: Use a 26-count tuple as the key for lowercase words, or a sorted-character key for general strings.
group-anagrams.complexity: O(total characters + 26n) expected time; O(26n) keys plus output references.

top-k-frequent-elements.goal: Find the k values with greatest frequency.
top-k-frequent-elements.approach: Count frequencies, then bucket values by count and scan buckets from high to low. A size-k heap is an alternative.
top-k-frequent-elements.complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space with buckets.
top-k-frequent-elements.edge: Ties and k equal to the number of distinct values.

product-of-array-except-self.goal: Compute each position’s product of all other elements without division.
product-of-array-except-self.approach: Write prefix products into output, then multiply by a running suffix product. Each answer combines the parts before and after its position.
product-of-array-except-self.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space excluding output.
product-of-array-except-self.edge: One zero, multiple zeros, and negative values.

valid-sudoku.goal: Check whether filled Sudoku cells violate row, column, or box uniqueness.
valid-sudoku.approach: Track seen digits separately for each row, column, and box. The box index is (row//3, column//3). This checks validity, not solvability.
valid-sudoku.complexity: O(1) for a fixed 9×9 board; generalized O(cells) time and space.
valid-sudoku.edge: Ignore empty cells; box duplicates can occur across different rows.

encode-and-decode-strings.goal: Encode a string list so every possible character can be decoded unambiguously.
encode-and-decode-strings.approach: Prefix each string with its length and a separator. Decode the numeric length, then consume exactly that many characters.
encode-and-decode-strings.complexity: O(total payload length + length headers) time and output space.
encode-and-decode-strings.edge: Empty strings, digits, and separator characters inside a string.

longest-consecutive-sequence.goal: Find the longest run of consecutive integer values, regardless of input order.
longest-consecutive-sequence.approach: Build a set. Start extending only at numbers whose predecessor is absent; each run is scanned once.
longest-consecutive-sequence.edge: Duplicates must not cause repeated run scans.

valid-palindrome.goal: Check whether alphanumeric characters form a palindrome ignoring case.
valid-palindrome.approach: Move inward from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters, and compare normalized characters.
valid-palindrome.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space for index-based scanning.

two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted.goal: Find two indices in a sorted array whose sum matches a target.
two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted.approach: Compare the end pair. A low sum rules out the left value; a high sum rules out the right value. Convert to the required one-based indices.

3sum.goal: List distinct value triplets whose sum is zero.
3sum.approach: Sort, fix one element, and use two pointers on the suffix. Skip repeated fixed values and repeated matched pointer values.
3sum.complexity: O(n²) time; sorting uses O(n) auxiliary space in Python, plus output.

container-with-most-water.goal: Choose two vertical lines enclosing the most water.
container-with-most-water.approach: Start at both ends. Move the shorter line: reducing width while keeping that limiting height cannot improve area.
container-with-most-water.edge: Equal heights and only two lines.

trapping-rain-water.goal: Compute water trapped between elevation bars.
trapping-rain-water.approach: Use two pointers with left and right maxima. Resolve the side with the smaller known maximum, whose water bound is already determined.
trapping-rain-water.edge: Monotonic heights trap nothing; interior dips can span many bars.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.goal: Maximize profit with one buy followed by one later sell.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.approach: Maintain the minimum price seen before or at the current day and the best nonnegative profit. Evaluate each sell against that minimum.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.edge: Strictly decreasing prices yield zero profit.

longest-substring-without-repeating-char.goal: Find the longest contiguous substring with all distinct characters.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.approach: Maintain a window and last-seen indices; jump left past a repeat, using max so left never moves backward.

longest-repeating-character-replacement.goal: Find the longest substring made uniform with at most k character replacements.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.approach: Track counts, window boundaries, and historical max frequency. Shrink when window length minus maxfreq exceeds k; stale maxfreq preserves the best length but not every window’s validity.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.edge: k=0 and windows whose historical dominant count becomes stale.

permutation-in-string.goal: Check whether a string contains a permutation of another as a substring.
permutation-in-string.approach: Maintain character counts in a fixed-size window equal to the pattern length. Compare with required frequencies, or track the number of matching counts.
permutation-in-string.complexity: O(n+m) for lowercase English letters; Counter comparisons cost O(alphabet) per window.
permutation-in-string.edge: Pattern longer than text and repeated letters.

minimum-window-substring.goal: Find the shortest substring covering every required character with multiplicity.
minimum-window-substring.approach: Expand counts until all required frequencies are satisfied, then shrink while valid and update the best range. Track satisfied distinct requirements carefully.
minimum-window-substring.complexity: O(n + m) expected time, O(alphabet) space.
minimum-window-substring.edge: Repeated requirements such as AABC; no valid window.

sliding-window-maximum.goal: Return the maximum in every fixed-width window.
sliding-window-maximum.approach: Use a deque of indices with decreasing values. Evict expired front indices and remove smaller or equal values from the back before adding the new index.
sliding-window-maximum.edge: Expired maxima, equal values, and k=1.

valid-parentheses.goal: Check that bracket types are correctly matched and nested.
valid-parentheses.approach: Push opening brackets. Every closing bracket must match the stack’s most recent opening bracket; the stack must be empty at the end.
valid-parentheses.edge: A closing bracket with an empty stack; leftover openings.

min-stack.goal: Support stack operations and minimum lookup in constant time.
min-stack.approach: Store each value together with the minimum up to that stack position. Popping restores the previous minimum automatically.
min-stack.complexity: O(1) per operation, O(n) stored entries.

evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.goal: Evaluate arithmetic written in postfix order.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.approach: Push operands. On an operator, pop right operand then left operand and push the result. Division must truncate toward zero.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.complexity: O(n) arithmetic operations, O(n) stack space.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.edge: Subtraction operand order and negative division.

generate-parentheses.goal: Generate all well-formed strings of n parenthesis pairs.
generate-parentheses.approach: Backtrack with counts of opens and closes. Add an opening if opens<n, and a closing only if closes<opens.
generate-parentheses.complexity: O(n × Cn) output work, O(n) auxiliary depth, where Cn is the nth Catalan number.
generate-parentheses.edge: Never allow a prefix with more closes than opens.

daily-temperatures.goal: For every day, find the wait until a strictly warmer day.
daily-temperatures.approach: Keep unresolved day indices in a nonincreasing-temperature stack. A warmer day resolves every colder index popped from the stack.

car-fleet.goal: Count groups of cars reaching a target without passing.
car-fleet.approach: Sort cars from closest to farthest from the target. A farther car joins the fleet ahead if its arrival time is no larger; otherwise it starts a new fleet.
car-fleet.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) sorting storage.
car-fleet.edge: Equal arrival times form one fleet.

largest-rectangle-in-histogram.goal: Find the maximum rectangle under contiguous histogram bars.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.approach: Keep increasing heights with their earliest possible start indices. A shorter bar finalizes popped heights; carry their earliest start forward, and flush at the end.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) stack space.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.edge: Equal heights, zero bars, and a rectangle ending at the final bar.

binary-search.goal: Find a target index in ascending sorted values.
binary-search.approach: Maintain an inclusive candidate interval, compare its midpoint, and discard mid with the impossible half. Return -1 after the interval becomes empty.
binary-search.edge: Empty input and a single candidate.

search-a-2d-matrix.goal: Find a target in a matrix whose row ranges are globally sorted.
search-a-2d-matrix.approach: Treat the matrix as one sorted array. Map flat midpoint m to row m//columns and column m%columns.
search-a-2d-matrix.edge: This does not apply to matrices with only independently sorted rows.

koko-eating-bananas.goal: Find the slowest integer eating speed finishing within h hours.
koko-eating-bananas.approach: Binary search the first feasible speed. Feasibility sums ceiling divisions for each positive pile; faster speeds cannot increase needed hours.
koko-eating-bananas.complexity: O(n log M) time with maximum pile M; O(1) space.
koko-eating-bananas.edge: Use ceiling division; h cannot be smaller than the number of positive piles.

find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.goal: Find the minimum in a rotated ascending array with distinct values.
find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.approach: Compare mid with right. If mid is larger, the minimum is strictly to its right; otherwise retain mid as the right boundary.
find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.edge: Already sorted input and a single element.

search-in-rotated-sorted-array.goal: Find a target in a rotated ascending array with distinct values.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.approach: At least one half is sorted. Check whether the target lies within that half’s value bounds, then keep the appropriate half.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.edge: Duplicates invalidate the simple distinct-value partition argument.

time-based-key-value-store.goal: Retrieve the most recent value for a key at or before a query time.
time-based-key-value-store.approach: Store each key’s increasing timestamp/value pairs. Binary search for the rightmost timestamp no greater than the query.
time-based-key-value-store.complexity: Set O(1) amortized; get O(log entries for key); O(total entries) space.
time-based-key-value-store.edge: A query before the first timestamp and a missing key.

median-of-two-sorted-arrays.goal: Find the median of two sorted arrays without merging all values.
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.approach: Binary search a partition of the shorter array, choosing the other partition so the left side has half the total elements. Require both left maxima ≤ opposite right minima.
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.edge: One empty array, odd/even total length, and partitions at array ends.

reverse-linked-list.goal: Reverse every next pointer and return the new head.
reverse-linked-list.approach: Save current.next, redirect current to prev, then advance both pointers. prev is always the reversed processed prefix.
reverse-linked-list.edge: Save the successor before overwriting the link.

merge-two-sorted-lists.goal: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
merge-two-sorted-lists.approach: Attach the smaller current node to a dummy-headed result and advance that source pointer. Attach the remaining suffix when one input ends.
merge-two-sorted-lists.complexity: O(n+m) time, O(1) auxiliary space when reusing nodes.

reorder-list.goal: Interleave a list’s front and back nodes in place.
reorder-list.approach: Find the midpoint, split the list, reverse the second half, then alternately weave nodes from both halves.
reorder-list.edge: Odd length; split the original link to prevent cycles.

remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.goal: Remove the nth node measured from the tail.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.approach: Use a dummy head and pointers separated by n nodes. When the leading pointer reaches the end, the trailing pointer identifies the predecessor to bypass.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.edge: Removing the head and a one-node list.

copy-list-with-random-pointer.goal: Deep-copy a list containing next and arbitrary random pointers.
copy-list-with-random-pointer.approach: Map each original node to its clone, then connect cloned next and random references in a second pass.
copy-list-with-random-pointer.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) map space plus copied nodes and serialization. Interleaving copies is an O(1)-auxiliary alternative.
copy-list-with-random-pointer.edge: Random pointers to self, earlier nodes, or null.

add-two-numbers.approach: Walk both lists with a carry. Emit total%10 and update carry=total//10 until both lists and carry are exhausted.
add-two-numbers.complexity: O(max(m,n)) time and output space, O(1) extra state.
add-two-numbers.edge: Different lengths and a final carry.

linked-list-cycle.goal: Determine whether following next pointers eventually loops.
linked-list-cycle.approach: Move slow one step and fast two steps. In a cycle their relative offset eventually reaches zero; otherwise fast reaches null.
linked-list-cycle.edge: Check fast and fast.next before advancing twice.

find-the-duplicate-number.goal: Find a repeated number among n+1 values in the range 1..n without modifying input.
find-the-duplicate-number.approach: Treat values as next indices. Floyd’s cycle algorithm locates the cycle entrance, which corresponds to the duplicate.
find-the-duplicate-number.edge: The proof relies on the 1..n value range and duplicate-number contract.

lru-cache.goal: Support constant-time lookup and least-recently-used eviction.
lru-cache.approach: Combine a key→node map with a doubly linked recency list. Move accessed nodes to the recent end and evict from the other end.
lru-cache.edge: Updating an existing key must also refresh recency.

merge-k-sorted-lists.approach: Put each list’s head into a min heap. Repeatedly remove the smallest node and insert its successor, using a tie-breaker for equal values.
merge-k-sorted-lists.complexity: O(N log k) time, O(k) auxiliary space for N total nodes.
merge-k-sorted-lists.edge: Empty lists and equal values with non-comparable node objects.

reverse-nodes-in-k-group.goal: Reverse complete groups of k nodes while leaving an incomplete final group unchanged.
reverse-nodes-in-k-group.approach: Check that a full group exists, reverse exactly that segment using its following node as the initial previous pointer, then reconnect both ends.
reverse-nodes-in-k-group.edge: k=1 and a final group shorter than k.

invert-binary-tree.goal: Swap the left and right children throughout a binary tree.
invert-binary-tree.approach: At each node, swap children and recursively invert both subtrees. Null nodes require no work.

maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.goal: Find the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.approach: Return zero for null and 1+max(left depth,right depth) for each nonempty node.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.edge: Node-count depth differs from edge-count height.

diameter-of-binary-tree.goal: Find the longest path between any two tree nodes, measured in edges.
diameter-of-binary-tree.approach: Postorder returns subtree height. At each node, left height plus right height is a path through it; update a separate global best.
diameter-of-binary-tree.edge: The longest path may not pass through the root.

balanced-binary-tree.goal: Check whether every node’s subtree heights differ by at most one.
balanced-binary-tree.approach: Postorder returns height or an unbalanced sentinel. Propagate failure immediately instead of recomputing heights separately for every node.
balanced-binary-tree.edge: A deep imbalance can exist even if root heights differ by one.

same-tree.goal: Check whether two trees have identical shape and values.
same-tree.approach: Pair nodes recursively: two nulls match, exactly one null fails, and nonnull nodes need equal values and both child pairs to match.
same-tree.complexity: O(min(n,m)) visited pairs until mismatch, O(h) stack.

subtree-of-another-tree.goal: Determine whether a complete subtree matches another tree.
subtree-of-another-tree.approach: At each candidate root, compare structure and values recursively. Serialization with unambiguous null tokens and linear matching is a more advanced alternative.
subtree-of-another-tree.complexity: Simple approach O(nm) worst-case, O(hn+hm) stack.
subtree-of-another-tree.edge: Matching root values alone is insufficient.

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.goal: Find the lowest node containing two targets below it in a BST.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.approach: If both targets are smaller, go left; if both larger, go right. The first split or target match is their lowest common ancestor.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.edge: A target node can be the ancestor of the other.

binary-tree-level-order-traversal.goal: Group tree values by depth from the root.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.approach: Use BFS, processing exactly the queue size recorded at the start of each level before appending the next level’s children.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.complexity: O(n) time, O(width) queue plus output.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.edge: Do not let newly appended children extend the current level’s loop.

binary-tree-right-side-view.goal: Return the visible value at every depth when looking from the right.
binary-tree-right-side-view.approach: BFS by level and record the last node in each level, or use right-first DFS and record the first node at each depth.
binary-tree-right-side-view.complexity: O(n) time, O(width) BFS queue or O(h) DFS stack.
binary-tree-right-side-view.edge: A left subtree can extend deeper than the right subtree.

count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.goal: Count nodes at least as large as every ancestor on their root path.
count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.approach: DFS carries the maximum value seen on the current root-to-node path. Count before updating the maximum for children.
count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.edge: Negative node values; initialize path maximum appropriately.

validate-binary-search-tree.goal: Verify strict BST ordering across whole subtrees.
validate-binary-search-tree.approach: Carry lower and upper bounds down recursion. A node must lie strictly between them; each child inherits and tightens one bound.
validate-binary-search-tree.edge: A node can satisfy its parent comparison but violate a distant ancestor’s bound.

kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.goal: Return the kth smallest BST value.
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.approach: Inorder traversal visits values in sorted order. Use an explicit stack and stop after popping k nodes.
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.edge: A skewed BST has h=n; k is one-based.

construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.goal: Reconstruct a tree from unique-value preorder and inorder traversals.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.approach: Preorder gives each subtree root. A value→inorder-index map splits left and right ranges; recurse using index bounds instead of slicing.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) map/stack space.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.edge: Unique values are needed for this reconstruction rule.

binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.goal: Find the maximum sum of any nonempty simple path in a tree.
binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.approach: Each node returns its best single downward branch. Update the global answer with node plus positive contributions from both children.
binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.edge: All-negative trees require initializing the answer below every value.

serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.goal: Encode a tree so its exact shape and values can be recovered.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.approach: Preorder serialization includes a null marker for every missing child. Deserialization consumes tokens recursively in the same order.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.complexity: O(n) time and serialized space, O(h) recursion.

implement-trie-prefix-tree.goal: Support inserting words, exact search, and prefix search.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.approach: Store one character per edge and a terminal marker per complete word. Exact search checks the marker; prefix search only requires a valid path.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.complexity: O(word length) expected per operation, O(total characters) space.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.edge: A word can also be another word’s prefix.

design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.goal: Search a word dictionary with a wildcard matching any one character.
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.approach: Insert words into a trie. Search follows one edge for a literal and recursively tries all children for a wildcard.
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.complexity: Literal search O(L); wildcard search visits matching trie branches, potentially exponential in L.
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.edge: A wildcard matches exactly one character, and the ending node must be terminal.

word-search-ii.goal: Find dictionary words formed by adjacent grid cells without reusing a cell in one path.
word-search-ii.approach: Build a trie and backtrack from each board cell, pruning when the path is not a prefix. Mark cells on the current path and restore them afterward.
word-search-ii.complexity: O(total word characters + RC·4^L + F log F) loose bound including sorting F found words; trie plus O(L) path state, excluding output.
word-search-ii.edge: Deduplicate found words; restore cells for later starting points.

kth-largest-element-in-a-stream.goal: Maintain the kth largest value as values arrive.
kth-largest-element-in-a-stream.approach: Keep a min heap of at most k values. Discard the smallest whenever size exceeds k; the root is the kth largest once k values exist.
kth-largest-element-in-a-stream.complexity: O(n) initialization plus O(n log(k+1)) trimming worst-case; O(log(k+1)) per addition. This constructor copies n values before trimming to k.
kth-largest-element-in-a-stream.edge: Duplicates count separately; fewer than k initial values.

last-stone-weight.goal: Repeatedly smash the two largest stones until at most one remains.
last-stone-weight.approach: Use a max heap via negated weights. Pop two, and push their positive difference if unequal.
last-stone-weight.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
last-stone-weight.edge: Equal stones both disappear; no stones returns zero.

k-closest-points-to-origin.goal: Return k points minimizing squared distance to the origin.
k-closest-points-to-origin.approach: Keep a max heap of size k keyed by squared distance, or quickselect. Square roots are unnecessary because they preserve distance order.
k-closest-points-to-origin.complexity: O(n log(k+1) + k log k) time including deterministic output sorting; O(k) selection storage.

kth-largest-element-in-an-array.goal: Find the kth largest element including duplicate occurrences.
kth-largest-element-in-an-array.approach: Quickselect partitions around a pivot and keeps only the side containing index n−k. A size-k min heap is a predictable alternative.
kth-largest-element-in-an-array.complexity: Quickselect expected O(n), worst O(n²); heap O(n log k).
kth-largest-element-in-an-array.edge: Randomize pivots or account for adversarial ordering.

task-scheduler.goal: Find the shortest schedule with a cooldown between equal tasks.
task-scheduler.approach: For unit tasks with a fixed cooldown, compare total tasks with the frame bound (maxfreq−1)×(cooldown+1)+number tied at maxfreq.
task-scheduler.complexity: O(n) time for a fixed alphabet, O(alphabet) space.
task-scheduler.edge: Cooldown zero and many task types filling all idle slots.

design-twitter.goal: Return recent posts from a user and followed users.
design-twitter.approach: Store timestamped posts per user. Merge followed users’ reverse chronological post streams with a heap, stopping after the feed limit.
design-twitter.complexity: O(F + K log F) feed time with heapify for F followed streams and K results; storage grows with posts.
design-twitter.edge: Include the user’s own posts; following/unfollowing must not duplicate streams.

find-median-from-data-stream.goal: Maintain the median after each inserted number.
find-median-from-data-stream.approach: Use a max heap for the lower half and min heap for the upper half. Maintain size difference at most one and all lower values ≤ all upper values.
find-median-from-data-stream.complexity: O(log n) insertion, O(1) median, O(n) space.
find-median-from-data-stream.edge: Negative values, equal values, and averaging for even size.

subsets.goal: Generate all subsets of distinct values.
subsets.approach: Record the current path, then choose each later index in turn. Copy the path when storing it and undo each choice afterward.
subsets.complexity: O(n2^n) output work, O(n) auxiliary depth.
subsets.edge: The empty subset must be included.

combination-sum.goal: List combinations of positive candidates summing to a target, allowing reuse.
combination-sum.approach: Backtrack with a starting candidate index and remaining target. Reusing keeps the same index; advancing indices avoids permutation duplicates.
combination-sum.complexity: Exponential search/output, depth up to target/minimum candidate.
combination-sum.edge: Candidates must be positive; stop or prune when the remaining target becomes negative.

permutations.goal: Generate all orderings of distinct values.
permutations.approach: Choose any unused index, recurse, then restore its used flag and path. A complete length-n path is one permutation.
permutations.complexity: O(n·n!) output work, O(n) auxiliary depth/state.
permutations.edge: Restore the used marker after returning.

subsets-ii.goal: Generate unique subsets when the input may contain duplicates.
subsets-ii.approach: Sort first. At a fixed recursion depth, skip a value equal to the previous candidate, while allowing equal values at deeper levels.
subsets-ii.complexity: O(n2^n) upper bound including output, O(n) depth plus sorting.
subsets-ii.edge: Skipping duplicates globally would wrongly omit subsets containing two copies.

combination-sum-ii.goal: List unique target-sum combinations when each input item can be used at most once.
combination-sum-ii.approach: Sort, skip equal sibling choices, and recurse from i+1 after taking item i. With positive values, stop when a candidate exceeds the remaining target.
combination-sum-ii.complexity: Exponential search/output, O(n) auxiliary depth plus sorting.
combination-sum-ii.edge: Duplicate values can be used when they come from different indices, but duplicate result lists must be avoided.

word-search.goal: Check whether a word can be formed by adjacent grid cells without reusing a cell.
word-search.approach: Backtrack over cell and word index. Mark the cell only for the active path, then restore it before exploring other branches.
word-search.complexity: O(RC·4^L) loose upper bound, O(L) recursion space.
word-search.edge: Reusing the same cell is forbidden even if the letter matches.

palindrome-partitioning.goal: List all partitions of a string into palindromic pieces.
palindrome-partitioning.approach: Backtrack over the next cut, accepting only palindromic pieces. Precomputing palindrome ranges avoids repeated checks.
palindrome-partitioning.complexity: O(n² + n2^n) upper bound including output with preprocessing; O(n²) table.
palindrome-partitioning.edge: Every single character is a valid palindrome; include the full remaining palindrome when valid.

letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.goal: Generate all letter strings represented by phone digits.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.approach: Backtrack one digit at a time using its letter choices, appending a result only after every digit is used.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.complexity: O(L·4^L) upper bound for time and stored strings; this iterative version retains a full frontier.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.edge: Empty digit input returns no combinations under the original problem contract.

n-queens.goal: Place n queens on an n×n board without shared rows, columns, or diagonals.
n-queens.approach: Place one queen per row. Track used columns, row−column diagonals, and row+column diagonals, restoring each on backtrack.
n-queens.complexity: Exponential search, commonly bounded by O(n!) placements plus board output; O(n) tracking.
n-queens.edge: Diagonal identifiers can be negative; n=2 and n=3 have no solutions.

number-of-islands.goal: Count connected components of land in a grid.
number-of-islands.approach: Scan cells; on unseen land, increment the count and flood-fill its entire four-direction component.
number-of-islands.complexity: O(RC) time and O(RC) visited/stack in the worst case.
number-of-islands.edge: Diagonal contact does not connect islands; mark on discovery.

clone-graph.goal: Deep-copy a connected graph while preserving cycles and shared neighbors.
clone-graph.approach: Map original node identity to its clone before recursing into neighbors. Reuse mapped clones whenever a node is encountered again.
clone-graph.complexity: O(V+E) time and O(V) map space plus output.
clone-graph.edge: Self-loops and equal node values require identity-based mapping.

max-area-of-island.goal: Find the largest connected land component by cell count.
max-area-of-island.approach: Flood-fill every unseen land component, count its cells, and keep the maximum.
max-area-of-island.complexity: O(RC) time, O(RC) worst-case auxiliary space.
max-area-of-island.edge: All water gives zero; four-direction adjacency only.

pacific-atlantic-water-flow.goal: Find cells from which water can reach both sets of ocean boundaries.
pacific-atlantic-water-flow.approach: Reverse the flow: start at each ocean’s border and traverse to equal or higher neighboring cells. Intersect the two reachable sets.
pacific-atlantic-water-flow.complexity: O(RC) traversal and space, plus O(K log K) to sort K output cells deterministically.
pacific-atlantic-water-flow.edge: Equal heights allow flow; reverse traversal must go uphill, not downhill.

surrounded-regions.goal: Capture O regions that are not connected to the border.
surrounded-regions.approach: First mark all O cells reachable from any border. Flip only unmarked O cells, then restore the border-connected marks.
surrounded-regions.complexity: O(RC) time and worst-case auxiliary space.
surrounded-regions.edge: A region connected by a narrow path to the border must remain unchanged.

rotting-oranges.goal: Find the minutes until all fresh oranges rot, or report impossibility.
rotting-oranges.approach: Multi-source BFS starts with every rotten orange at time zero. Each layer rots adjacent fresh cells; count remaining fresh cells.
rotting-oranges.edge: No fresh oranges means zero; unreachable fresh oranges mean -1.

walls-and-gates.goal: Fill each empty room with its distance to the nearest gate.
walls-and-gates.approach: Run one multi-source BFS from all gates. The first visit assigns the shortest distance; walls block edges.
walls-and-gates.complexity: O(RC) time and O(RC) queue space.
walls-and-gates.edge: Do not run a separate full BFS from every room.

course-schedule.goal: Determine whether directed prerequisites permit completing all courses.
course-schedule.approach: Use topological sorting and check whether all vertices are processed, or use DFS with visiting/done states to detect directed cycles.
course-schedule.edge: A visited set alone cannot distinguish a current-path cycle from a finished vertex.

course-schedule-ii.goal: Return a valid order respecting all course prerequisites.
course-schedule-ii.approach: Build edges from prerequisite to dependent. Kahn’s algorithm outputs zero-indegree vertices; if fewer than all courses are output, return no order.
course-schedule-ii.edge: Include courses with no edges and reject a partial cyclic order.

redundant-connection.goal: Find the edge creating a cycle in an otherwise tree-like undirected graph.
redundant-connection.approach: Use Union-Find; the first edge whose endpoints already share a root closes a cycle.
redundant-connection.complexity: O(E α(V)) amortized time, O(V) space.
redundant-connection.edge: Labels may be one-based; allocate or normalize accordingly.

number-of-connected-components-in-an-und.goal: Count connected groups including isolated vertices.
number-of-connected-components-in-an-und.approach: Flood-fill from every unvisited vertex, or start with n components and decrement on each successful Union-Find merge.
number-of-connected-components-in-an-und.complexity: DFS/BFS O(V+E); Union-Find O((V+E)α(V)); O(V) extra storage.
number-of-connected-components-in-an-und.edge: Isolated vertices each count as a component.

graph-valid-tree.goal: Check whether an undirected graph is a single tree.
graph-valid-tree.approach: Require n−1 edges and connectivity. A traversal or Union-Find can verify connectivity; alternatively detect cycles explicitly and check all nodes reached.
graph-valid-tree.complexity: O(V + E·α(V)) amortized time and O(V) space for Union-Find.
graph-valid-tree.edge: Acyclic but disconnected is a forest, not a tree.

word-ladder.goal: Find the shortest sequence of single-letter changes through allowed words.
word-ladder.approach: BFS over words, generating one-character replacements and checking a word set. Mark discovered words immediately; bidirectional BFS can reduce exploration.
word-ladder.complexity: With alphabet A and length L, O(N·A·L²) using copied strings; storage O(NL).
word-ladder.edge: The end word must be reachable through the dictionary; count words, not just transformations, per prompt.

reconstruct-itinerary.goal: Use every directed flight exactly once in a lexicographically smallest valid itinerary from JFK.
reconstruct-itinerary.approach: Sort destinations in reverse lexical order and apply Hierholzer’s algorithm: remove the smallest unused edge, then append airports on backtracking and reverse the result.
reconstruct-itinerary.complexity: O(E log E) sorting time, O(E) storage.
reconstruct-itinerary.edge: Greedily appending the smallest destination can strand unused flights; postorder is essential.

min-cost-to-connect-all-points.goal: Connect all points with minimum total Manhattan distance.
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.approach: Use Prim’s MST algorithm with an array of best connection costs. Each iteration picks the cheapest unused point and relaxes all remaining points.
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.complexity: O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space without building every edge.
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.edge: The cheapest edge from each point independently does not guarantee a connected minimum tree.

network-delay-time.goal: Find when every vertex receives a signal through nonnegative weighted directed edges.
network-delay-time.approach: Run Dijkstra from the source. Return the maximum shortest distance, or -1 if any vertex is unreachable.
network-delay-time.complexity: O((V+E) log(E+1)) with a lazy heap; O(V+E) storage.
network-delay-time.edge: Skip stale heap entries; a first discovered route need not be shortest.

swim-in-rising-water.goal: Minimize the highest elevation encountered on a grid path.
swim-in-rising-water.approach: Use Dijkstra with path cost max(current cost,next elevation), or binary search water level with reachability checks.
swim-in-rising-water.complexity: Heap approach O(RC log(RC)) time, O(RC) space.
swim-in-rising-water.edge: This is a bottleneck cost, not the sum of elevations.

alien-dictionary.goal: Infer a character order consistent with lexicographically sorted words.
alien-dictionary.approach: Compare adjacent words and add an edge at their first differing character. Include every character, reject an invalid prefix order, then topologically sort.
alien-dictionary.complexity: O(total characters + E + V log V + Σ d log d) with deterministic sorting of ready characters and neighbor sets; O(V+E) space.
alien-dictionary.edge: A longer word before its exact prefix is invalid; deduplicate edges before incrementing indegree.

cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.goal: Find a minimum-price route using at most k intermediate stops.
cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.approach: Perform k+1 relaxation rounds, each reading only the previous distance array and writing into a copy. The snapshot enforces the edge budget.
cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.edge: In-place updates can silently traverse multiple edges in a single round.

climbing-stairs.goal: Count ways to reach stair n with steps of one or two.
climbing-stairs.approach: ways[i]=ways[i−1]+ways[i−2]. Define base cases consistently; keeping only the last two values gives constant auxiliary space.
climbing-stairs.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space for fixed-width counts.
climbing-stairs.edge: One stair and the chosen interpretation of zero stairs.

min-cost-climbing-stairs.goal: Reach the top with minimum paid step cost, starting at step 0 or 1.
min-cost-climbing-stairs.approach: Let dp[i] be minimum cost to reach position i. Transition from i−1 paying cost[i−1] or i−2 paying cost[i−2]; dp[0]=dp[1]=0.
min-cost-climbing-stairs.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space with two rolling values.
min-cost-climbing-stairs.edge: The top is beyond the last array index and has no extra cost.

house-robber.goal: Maximize the sum of selected values with no adjacent selections.
house-robber.approach: For each house, compare skipping it with taking it plus the best value two houses earlier. Maintain the previous two DP results.
house-robber.edge: Single house and a tempting large value surrounded by valuable neighbors.

house-robber-ii.goal: Maximize nonadjacent selections when first and last houses are adjacent.
house-robber-ii.approach: Solve two linear cases: exclude the first house or exclude the last. Take the larger result; handle a singleton separately.
house-robber-ii.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space for copied slices; index ranges can reduce extra space to O(1).
house-robber-ii.edge: Taking both endpoints violates the circular constraint.

longest-palindromic-substring.approach: Expand around each character and each gap between characters. Every palindrome has one of these odd/even centers.
longest-palindromic-substring.complexity: O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space excluding returned substring.

palindromic-substrings.approach: Expand around each odd and even center, incrementing the count for each matching expansion.
palindromic-substrings.edge: Equal-valued substrings at different positions count separately.

decode-ways.goal: Count valid ways to interpret digits as values 1 through 26.
decode-ways.approach: A state at i sums one-digit and valid two-digit continuations. A leading zero contributes zero; the empty suffix contributes one completed decoding.
decode-ways.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) rolling space or O(n) table.
decode-ways.edge: 0 cannot decode alone; 10 is valid, 06 is not.

coin-change.goal: Find the fewest reusable positive coins making an exact amount.
coin-change.approach: dp[0]=0; for each amount, try one coin plus the optimal smaller remainder. Unreachable states stay infinite.
coin-change.complexity: O(amount × coin types) time, O(amount) space.

maximum-product-subarray.goal: Find the greatest product of a nonempty contiguous subarray.
maximum-product-subarray.approach: Maintain both maximum and minimum products ending here, since a negative multiplier swaps their roles. Include starting fresh at the current value.
maximum-product-subarray.edge: Zeros reset products; two negatives can form the maximum.

word-break.goal: Check whether a string can be segmented into dictionary words.
word-break.approach: dp[i] marks whether prefix s[:i] is segmentable. For each endpoint, check dictionary words or valid earlier split positions.
word-break.complexity: O(n·L²) worst-case with Python substring creation, where L is maximum word length; O(n) DP plus dictionary storage.
word-break.edge: A valid short prefix may lead to a dead end; do not commit greedily.

longest-increasing-subsequence.goal: Find the longest strictly increasing subsequence length.
longest-increasing-subsequence.approach: Maintain tails[len−1], the smallest possible ending value for an increasing subsequence of that length. Replace using lower_bound, or append if larger than all tails.
longest-increasing-subsequence.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
longest-increasing-subsequence.edge: Equal values replace rather than extend; tails itself is not necessarily the final subsequence.

partition-equal-subset-sum.goal: Determine whether values split into two equal-sum subsets.
partition-equal-subset-sum.approach: If the total is odd, fail. Otherwise solve 0/1 subset-sum for half the total, updating reachable sums downward so each item is used once.
partition-equal-subset-sum.complexity: O(n × total sum) time, O(total sum) space.
partition-equal-subset-sum.edge: Forward in-place updates would reuse an item multiple times.

unique-paths.goal: Count right/down paths from the top-left to bottom-right of a grid.
unique-paths.approach: Each cell receives ways from above plus left. Initialize the first row/column to one, or use a rolling row.
unique-paths.complexity: O(RC) time, O(C) auxiliary space with rolling DP.
unique-paths.edge: One row or one column has exactly one path.

longest-common-subsequence.goal: Find the longest order-preserving common subsequence of two strings.
longest-common-subsequence.approach: State (i,j) represents remaining suffixes. Equal characters contribute 1+diagonal; otherwise skip either character and take the maximum.
longest-common-subsequence.complexity: O(mn) time and O(mn) table space; rows can be compressed.
longest-common-subsequence.edge: Subsequence allows gaps; substring does not.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo.goal: Maximize stock profit with a one-day cooldown after selling.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo.approach: Track holding, just-sold, and resting states. Buy only from the previous resting state, so yesterday’s sale cannot fund today’s purchase.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) rolling state space.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo.edge: Compute all new states from old snapshots, not partially updated values.

coin-change-ii.goal: Count unordered combinations of reusable coins forming an amount.
coin-change-ii.approach: Initialize ways[0]=1. Loop coin types outside and amounts upward inside, adding ways[a−coin] to ways[a].
coin-change-ii.complexity: O(amount × coin types) time, O(amount) space.
coin-change-ii.edge: Reversing the loop roles can count permutations instead of combinations.

target-sum.goal: Count sign assignments producing a target sum.
target-sum.approach: Memoize (index,current sum), exploring plus and minus for each value. A subset-sum transformation is also possible when parity and range conditions hold.
target-sum.complexity: O(nS) time and O(S) rolling-map space for reachable sum range S.
target-sum.edge: Zero values produce two distinct sign choices even though sums are equal.

interleaving-string.goal: Check whether two strings interleave to form a third while preserving each source’s order.
interleaving-string.approach: After a length check, DP over consumed counts (i,j); next target index is i+j, and either source may supply the next matching character.
interleaving-string.complexity: O(mn) time and O(n) rolling space, where n is the second string length.
interleaving-string.edge: Identical next characters require exploring both possibilities.

longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.goal: Find the longest strictly increasing orthogonal grid path.
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.approach: Memoize the longest path starting at each cell. Only traverse to strictly larger neighbors; this makes the implicit graph acyclic.
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.edge: No global visited prohibition is needed across independent starts; cache results instead.

distinct-subsequences.goal: Count subsequences of a source string equal to a target string.
distinct-subsequences.approach: DP tracks source and target positions. Skip the source character, and also match it when equal. An empty target has one matching subsequence.
distinct-subsequences.complexity: O(mn) time; O(n) rolling space with backward target updates.
distinct-subsequences.edge: A source shorter than target cannot match; repeated letters create multiple index choices.

edit-distance.goal: Find minimum insertions, deletions, and replacements transforming one string into another.
edit-distance.approach: State (i,j) represents remaining suffixes. Equal characters advance both; otherwise add one to the minimum of insert, delete, and replace transitions.
edit-distance.complexity: O(mn) time and O(mn) space, reducible to rolling rows.
edit-distance.edge: Empty suffix cost is the remaining opposite length.

burst-balloons.goal: Maximize coins from removing balloons whose current neighbors determine reward.
burst-balloons.approach: Add boundary 1s and use interval DP. Choose which balloon is removed last inside each interval, leaving its outside neighbors fixed.
burst-balloons.edge: Choosing the first balloon leaves changing neighbors; choosing the last makes subproblems independent.

regular-expression-matching.goal: Match a whole string against a pattern with dot and star operators.
regular-expression-matching.approach: Memoize (text index,pattern index). For x*, either skip the pair or consume one matching character while keeping the same pattern position.
regular-expression-matching.edge: Star modifies its preceding token; this is not shell-glob matching.

maximum-subarray.goal: Find the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous subarray.
maximum-subarray.approach: Kadane’s algorithm chooses whether to extend the best subarray ending previously or restart at the current value. Track the best ending anywhere.
maximum-subarray.edge: All-negative input must return the largest element, not zero.

jump-game.goal: Determine whether forward jumps can reach the last index.
jump-game.approach: Maintain the farthest reachable index. If the scan reaches an index beyond it, progress is impossible; otherwise extend reach from that position.
jump-game.edge: Zeros can create an unreachable gap.

jump-game-ii.goal: Find the minimum number of jumps to reach the final index.
jump-game-ii.approach: Treat reachable indices as BFS layers represented by ranges. Scan one range to find the next farthest boundary, then increment the jump count.
jump-game-ii.edge: Do not add an extra jump when already at the last index; original inputs guarantee reachability.

gas-station.goal: Find a starting station that can complete a circular route, if one exists.
gas-station.approach: If total gas minus cost is negative, fail. When a running segment balance goes negative, no start inside that segment can work; reset to the next station.
gas-station.edge: The candidate must still satisfy the total-balance check.

hand-of-straights.goal: Partition cards into equal-sized groups of consecutive values.
hand-of-straights.approach: Count cards and process values in ascending order. Every remaining smallest card must start a group; consume one count at each next required value.
hand-of-straights.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space with sorted keys/counts.
hand-of-straights.edge: Total card count must be divisible by group size; duplicates require multiple groups.

merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet.goal: Check whether componentwise maxima of chosen triplets can equal a target.
merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet.approach: Ignore triplets exceeding the target in any coordinate. Among the remaining triplets, record which target coordinates are matched exactly.
merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space for three coordinates.
merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet.edge: One too-large coordinate makes that entire triplet unusable.

partition-labels.goal: Split a string into the most parts so each character appears in only one part.
partition-labels.approach: Record each character’s last position. Scan and extend the current partition end to all encountered last positions; close when the scan reaches that end.
partition-labels.edge: A character seen early may force a much later boundary.

valid-parenthesis-string.goal: Determine whether parentheses and wildcard stars can form a balanced sequence.
valid-parenthesis-string.approach: Track minimum and maximum possible unmatched opens. Update both for each character, clamp minimum to zero, and fail if maximum goes negative.
valid-parenthesis-string.edge: A star may be empty, opening, or closing; final minimum must be zero.

insert-interval.goal: Insert a new interval into sorted nonoverlapping intervals and merge overlap.
insert-interval.approach: Copy intervals ending before the new start, merge all touching intervals into the new range, then append the untouched suffix.
insert-interval.edge: New interval before all, after all, or containing many intervals.

merge-intervals.goal: Return the union of possibly overlapping closed intervals.
merge-intervals.approach: Sort by start; merge into the last output range when the next start is at most its end. Extend by max of ends.
merge-intervals.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) sorting/output space.
merge-intervals.edge: Contained intervals must not shrink the merged end.

non-overlapping-intervals.goal: Remove the fewest intervals so the remaining intervals do not overlap.
non-overlapping-intervals.approach: Maximize retained intervals by earliest finish time, then subtract that count from n. An exchange argument justifies taking the earliest-finishing compatible interval.
non-overlapping-intervals.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) sorting storage.
non-overlapping-intervals.edge: Touching endpoints are compatible under the usual prompt convention.

meeting-rooms.goal: Check whether one person can attend every meeting.
meeting-rooms.approach: Sort by start and check each start against the previous end. Any strict overlap proves a conflict.
meeting-rooms.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) sorting storage.
meeting-rooms.edge: A meeting starting exactly when another ends is allowed.

meeting-rooms-ii.goal: Find the minimum number of rooms needed for all meetings.
meeting-rooms-ii.approach: Sort starts and ends separately or maintain a min heap of active end times. The answer is the maximum number of simultaneous meetings.
meeting-rooms-ii.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
meeting-rooms-ii.edge: Process an ending before a starting event at the same time.

minimum-interval-to-include-each-query.goal: For each query value, find the shortest closed interval containing it.
minimum-interval-to-include-each-query.approach: Sort intervals by start and queries by value. Add eligible intervals to a min heap keyed by length; discard expired heap roots before answering.
minimum-interval-to-include-each-query.complexity: O((n+q) log n + q log q) time, O(n+q) space.
minimum-interval-to-include-each-query.edge: Restore original query order; inclusive interval length is end−start+1.

rotate-image.goal: Rotate a square matrix 90 degrees clockwise in place.
rotate-image.approach: Transpose across the main diagonal once, then reverse each row. The coordinate mapping is (r,c)→(c,n−1−r).
rotate-image.edge: Swapping both diagonal halves cancels the transpose.

spiral-matrix.goal: List matrix values in clockwise spiral order.
spiral-matrix.approach: Maintain top, bottom, left, and right boundaries. Consume one side at a time and shrink its boundary, checking bounds before opposite sides.
spiral-matrix.complexity: O(RC) time, O(1) auxiliary space excluding output.
spiral-matrix.edge: A remaining single row or column must not be read twice.

set-matrix-zeroes.goal: Zero every row and column containing an original zero.
set-matrix-zeroes.approach: Use the first row and column as markers, with separate flags for whether those first boundaries originally contained zero. Apply markers only after scanning.
set-matrix-zeroes.edge: Writing zeros during initial scanning can create false markers.

happy-number.goal: Determine whether repeated sums of squared digits eventually reach 1.
happy-number.approach: Treat each number as a node pointing to its digit-square sum. Detect a cycle with a set or Floyd’s fast/slow pointers.
happy-number.complexity: Each transform costs O(number of digits); the sequence quickly enters a bounded range. Floyd uses O(1) state.
happy-number.edge: A cycle excluding 1 means the number is not happy.

plus-one.goal: Increment a nonnegative integer stored as decimal digits.
plus-one.approach: Scan from the last digit. If it is below 9, increment and return; otherwise write zero and carry. Prepend one if all digits were 9.
plus-one.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) output/copy storage; digit processing itself uses O(1) state.

powx-n.goal: Compute x raised to an integer exponent efficiently.
powx-n.approach: Use exponentiation by squaring. Multiply the result for set exponent bits, square the base, and halve the exponent. Invert the base for negative exponents.
powx-n.complexity: O(log abs(n)) multiplications, O(1) iterative space.
powx-n.edge: n=0; negative exponents; zero base with negative exponent is undefined.

multiply-strings.goal: Multiply two nonnegative decimal strings without converting whole strings to integers.
multiply-strings.approach: Accumulate each digit-pair product at positions i+j and i+j+1, propagate carries, and strip leading zeros.
multiply-strings.edge: Any zero input must produce exactly "0".

detect-squares.goal: Count axis-aligned squares formed with a query point and stored points.
detect-squares.approach: Count point multiplicities. For each stored point diagonally opposite the query with equal nonzero horizontal and vertical offsets, multiply counts of the other two corners and the diagonal point.
detect-squares.complexity: Add expected O(1); query O(number of distinct stored points); O(distinct points) space.
detect-squares.edge: Repeated points multiply the number of squares; zero side length is invalid.

single-number.goal: Find the unique value when every other value occurs exactly twice.
single-number.approach: XOR all values: associativity and commutativity allow equal pairs to cancel, leaving the singleton.
single-number.complexity: O(n) fixed-width operations, O(1) auxiliary space.
single-number.edge: The cancellation rule changes if other values occur three times.

number-of-1-bits.goal: Count set bits in an unsigned fixed-width integer.
number-of-1-bits.approach: Repeatedly clear the lowest set bit with n &= n−1 and count iterations.
number-of-1-bits.complexity: O(number of set bits) time, O(1) fixed-width space.
number-of-1-bits.edge: Python negative integers need masking before using this unsigned-bit method.

counting-bits.goal: Return the number of set bits for each integer from zero through n.
counting-bits.approach: bits[i]=bits[i>>1]+(i&1). Each number reuses the count of its right-shifted smaller value.
counting-bits.edge: The base case bits[0] is zero.

reverse-bits.goal: Reverse all bits of a fixed-width unsigned integer.
reverse-bits.approach: Repeat exactly 32 times: shift the result left, append the current low bit, and shift the input right.
reverse-bits.complexity: O(32) time, O(1) space under the 32-bit contract.
reverse-bits.edge: Leading zeros must be processed; stopping when n becomes zero is wrong.

missing-number.goal: Find the absent value from distinct values covering 0..n except one.
missing-number.approach: XOR all expected indices 0..n and all present values, or subtract the actual sum from n(n+1)/2.
missing-number.edge: The missing value may be zero or n.

sum-of-two-integers.goal: Add signed integers using bit operations rather than arithmetic addition.
sum-of-two-integers.approach: XOR computes sum without carry; AND then left-shift computes carry. Repeat with a fixed-width mask and convert the final bit pattern to a signed value.
sum-of-two-integers.complexity: O(word width) worst-case iterations, O(1) fixed-width space.
sum-of-two-integers.edge: Python’s unbounded negative integers require explicit masking and signed conversion.

reverse-integer.goal: Reverse decimal digits of a signed 32-bit integer, returning zero on overflow.
reverse-integer.approach: Separate the sign, repeatedly extract digits, and check against the signed 32-bit bound before appending each digit. Restore the sign afterward.
reverse-integer.complexity: O(decimal digits) time, O(1) fixed-width space.
reverse-integer.edge: Trailing zeros disappear; the negative bound has magnitude 2^31, one greater than the positive bound.
